title: The Normal Distribution
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Maths: Normal Distribution Worksheets
standard_text: Understand and use the normal distribution as a model; find probabilities using the normal distribution; link to histograms, mean, standard deviation and points of inflection; select an appropriate probability distribution for a context.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level maths worksheets on the normal distribution: z-values, probabilities, the 68–95–99.7 rule, comparing scores and real-life normal models. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: About 68% of values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean.
body_html:
How it works

X ~ N(μ, σ²) is symmetrical about μ. Standardise with z = (x − μ)/σ. About 68% of values lie within μ ± σ, 95% within μ ± 2σ and 99.7% within μ ± 3σ.

Example

μ = 50, σ = 4. z for x = 58?

(58 − 50) ÷ 4

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by the variance instead of the standard deviation.
  • Forgetting the symmetry: P(z > −a) = P(z < a).
  • Using N(μ, σ) when σ² is given.

faq.a: A normal distribution with mean μ and variance σ². The standard deviation is σ.

faq.q: How do you compare scores from two normal distributions?
faq.a: Work out the z-value of each. The larger z-value is the better relative score.

items.q: A normal distribution has mean 12 and standard deviation 2. What percent of the data is above 14?
items.e: 14 is 1 SD above the mean. 68% is within 1 SD, so 32% is outside, split equally between the two tails: 16%.

items.q: Light bulb lifetimes are normally distributed with mean 800 hours and standard deviation 50 hours. What is the probability that a bulb lasts less than 750 hours?
items.e: 750 is 1 SD below the mean. 34% is between it and the mean, so 50% − 34% = 16% is below it. About 0.16.

items.q: A normal distribution has mean 100 and standard deviation 15. What percent of the data is above 130?
items.e: 130 is 2 SD above the mean. 95% is within 2 SD, so 5% is outside, split equally between the two tails: 2.5%.

items.q: Test scores are normally distributed with mean 500 and standard deviation 100. A student scores 700. About what percentile is this?
items.e: 700 is 2 SD above the mean, and 97.5% of scores are below it. About the 97.5th percentile.
